column1: # GENERATION, KEYED: pack(d, t, k), task C2 of
# argument, each member's child stands under the key `k` answers for that
# member, in place of the member's own key or text. Columns:
# name<TAB>mode<TAB>src<TAB>expect. Each expectation is what both engines
# `k` is read once for each member, where the member's child would stand
# under its own key: `_` is the member and `key(0)` its own key, or its
# position in a list. It must settle to a string, or the call is
# `pack_key`. `t` is read at the child's place, as without `k`, so its
# `key(0)` is the key `k` answered. Children whose keys collide unify.
# The plan's two idioms: a map keyed by a field, and by two joined.

column3: xs: [{ns: a, name: web, port: 80}, {ns: b, name: db, port: 5432}]\nbyname: pack($.xs, _, at(_, name))
xs: [{name: web, port: 80}, {name: db, port: 5432}]\nbyname: pack($.xs, _, at(_, name))
xs: [{ns: a, name: web, port: 80}, {ns: b, name: db, port: 5432}]\nports: pack($.xs, at(_, port), at(_, ns) + "/" + at(_, name))
xs: [{ns: a, name: web, port: 80}, {ns: b, name: db, port: 5432}]\nports: pack($.xs, at(_, port), at(_, ns) + "/" + at(_, name))

column1: # key(0) is the member's own key in a map, its position in a list.

column3: m: {a: {id: x}, b: {id: y}}\nout: pack($.m, at(_, id), at(_, id) + "-" + key(0))

column1: # key() reads the level above, the call's own key, as elsewhere.
# An inverted map, once each member carries its key: t reads key(0) at
# the child's place, where it is the key k answered.

column3: m: {a: x, b: y}\nst: hide(pack($.m, {k: key(), v: _}))\nout: pack($.st, at(_, k), at(_, v))
m: {a: x, b: y}\nout: pack(pack($.m, {k: key(1), v: _}), at(_, k), at(_, v))
m: {a: x, b: y}\nout: pack($.m, key(0), _)

column1: # Over a list the members need not be strings, since k makes the key.

column3: xs: [{n: "a b", v: 1}]\nout: pack($.xs, at(_, v), at(_, n))
names: {x: web, y: db}\nm: {x: 80, y: 5432}\nout: pack($.m, _, at($.names, key(0)))
p: "x-"\nxs: [{n: a}, {n: b}]\nout: pack($.xs, _, $.p + at(_, n))

column1: # Keys that collide unify, as without k.

column3: xs: [{n: a, v: 1}, {n: a, w: 2}, {n: b, v: 3}]\nout: pack($.xs, _, at(_, n))
xs: [{n: a, v: 1}, {n: a, v: 2}]\nout: pack($.xs, _, at(_, n))

column1: # A key that is not a string: a number, a kind, a choice, a map.
# A field that is not there: at refuses it as no_path, at the call.
# Under maybe it is absence, and absence is no string.
# A marked member is skipped, as without k; a marked field is read by at

column3: m: {a: {n: p}, b: hide({n: q})}\nout: pack($.m, _, at(_, n))
m: {a: {n: hide(p), v: 1}}\nout: pack($.m, _, at(_, n))
m: {a: {n: type(p), v: 1}}\nout: pack($.m, at(_, v), at(_, n))

column1: # A relative path in k does not name the member's field (ruling 7): it
# reads from where the child would stand under its own key, as one in t
# does, so `.n` reads the output being made, which waits on the call.

column3: g: {x: {items: [{id: p}, {id: q}]}}\nout: pack($.g, pack(at(_, items), 1, at(_, id)))
xs: [{kids: [{n: a}]}, {kids: [{n: b}]}]\nout: each($.xs, pack(at(_, kids), _, at(_, n)))
xs: [{n: a, k: 1}, {n: b, k: 2}]\nout: filter(pack($.xs, _, at(_, n)), {k: 2})
xs: [{n: a}, {n: b}]\nout: pack($.xs, {r: *1 | integer}, at(_, n))\nout: b: r: 5
xs: [{n: a, v: 1}]\nout: pack($.xs, at(_, v), at(_, n))\ne: $.out.a
